use: how a safeguard works, from a company notice
request: Our IT team sent this notice. Make a 25 second explainer for staff on why two-factor matters, based on it.

material.name: it-notice.txt
material.text: From Monday all staff accounts require two-factor sign-in. After your password, the site sends a six-digit code to your registered phone. A stolen or leaked password alone will no longer let anyone into your account, because the attacker would also need your phone. Never share the code with anyone, including IT.

topic: How two-factor login stops a stolen password
intent: Everyday users want to know why turning on two-factor matters.
goal: The viewer knows the two factors and why a stolen password alone fails.
promise: A stolen password that still doesn't open the door.
arc: A stolen password, two keys, the code going to the phone, the thief stuck.

events.text: Someone steals your password. With two-factor login, they still can't get in. Here's why.
Logging in asks for two things: something you know, your password, and something you have, your phone.
events.knows: Two factors: something you know and something you have.
events.look: the two keys: password and phone

events.text: The thief has the password. The site sends a code to your phone, which the thief doesn't have.
events.knows: The code goes to the phone the thief lacks.
events.look: the code going to your phone, not to the thief

holds.does: the code sits on your phone while the thief's login waits, stuck

events.text: One stolen key isn't enough. They'd need both.

quiz.q: What two things does login ask for?
quiz.a: Something you know (the password) and something you have (the phone).

quiz.q: Where does the site send the code?
Why can't the thief log in?
quiz.a: They have only the password, not the phone that gets the code.

quiz.q: What happened to the thief's login on screen?
quiz.a: It was stuck, waiting for the code; the lock stayed shut.

quiz.q: Per the notice, what does the site send after the password?
quiz.a: A six-digit code to your registered phone.
